deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a draft letter in ink with pencil additions. A pencil heading at the top reads roughly 'Auf den [...] erlauben sich die Unterzeichneten Nachfolgendes unterthänigst zu erwiedern'. This is the standard opening formula of a joint expert report ('the undersigned humbly beg to reply as follows'), and it is presumably a draft opening for the report itself.

The letter body is in ink and addressed to 'Hochgeehrter Herr Professor!'. Riemann writes that after careful consideration he has become convinced that he cannot sign the report the Professor drafted on the investigation of a Central European arc measurement ('mitteleuropäische Gradmessung'). He therefore has no choice but to write a separate report to the Royal Curatorium ('Königliches Curatorium', the Göttingen university authority under the Hanoverian government). So as not to delay the matter further, he has given the joint report to a copyist for fair copying. The copy is to omit his name from the heading and include the changes the Professor asked for. The copyist has finished the first two pages, and Riemann awaits further instructions. It is signed 'Ganz Ihr ergebenster B. Riemann, Göttingen, den 5. October 1861'.

Below the signature are pencil drafts, heavily struck through, apparently for Riemann's separate report. They contain:
- the phrase 'würde es jedoch eine Geringschätzung dieser Bedenken [sein], wenn ...';
- several attempts at a sentence saying that the manner in which the arc-measurement data could provide a basis for a more exact investigation of the figure of the Earth would depend on the outcome of these negotiations ('Verhandlungen').

Context: in 1861 J. J. Baeyer proposed a Central European arc measurement, the origin of the later Internationale Erdmessung. German states, including Hanover, solicited expert opinions. Riemann evidently dissented from a colleague's draft opinion. The colleague is possibly W. Weber or another Göttingen professor; the identity is not determinable from this page.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated. The previous page holds a fragment of a second-order elliptic operator in divergence form, sum over i,j of d/dx_i(a_ij du/dx_j). The next page holds geometric sketches. No derivation exists on this page to reconstruct.

results.what: Biographical/administrative document: Riemann declines to co-sign a joint report on Baeyer's proposed Central European arc measurement (Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung) and announces a separate report to the Königliches Curatorium, dated Göttingen 5 Oct 1861.
results.modern_name: Expert opinion (Gutachten) on the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (precursor of the International Association of Geodesy)

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematical content. It is a historically interesting letter draft documenting Riemann's dissent on the 1861 Gradmessung report. It is of minor biographical interest, and his involvement in geodetic expert opinions may already be known to Riemann scholars.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably reads 'Auf den' (followed by a gap for the title of the request), not 'Auf dem'.
The first struck-through line under the salutation is an earlier start of 'Nach reiflicher Erwägung'. This is consistent with the transcription.
In 'über die [-Lage-] Untersuchung' the struck word is uncertain and may be 'Frage'.
'habe ich Schüler [?]' is uncertain. It most likely names or describes the copyist, given 'Dieser hat ... abgeschrieben'.
The signature reads 'B. Riemann', preceded by 'Ihr ergebenster', and the date 'Göttingen, den 5. October 1861'. This is consistent with the transcription.
The pencil fragment reads 'würde es jedoch eine Geringschätzung dieser Bedenken [sein], wenn ...'. It is a draft for the separate report, not part of the letter.
